result_text:
Conversion fell mostly because a new landing page, `/lp/summer-sale`, started sending traffic on 2026-06-08. It converts at about 0.5%, and the pages that existed in week 1 converted the same as before. This is an association, not a proven cause, because nothing randomized who landed on the new page.

**What the numbers show**
- **Your 2.5% is a checkout-reached rate.** It is `checkout_reached` sessions divided by sessions: 3.12% in week 1 and 2.51% in week 2. Orders divided by sessions gives 3.12% and 2.76%, because the session log is incomplete on 06-13 and 06-14 (see below).
- **The new page is the drop.** In 06-08 to 06-12 it received 160 sessions a day, about 20% of traffic. It reached checkout in 4 of 800 sessions (0.5%), against 3.10% for the other pages.
- **The old pages did not change.** In week 2 they converted at 3.10%, against 3.12% in week 1. Putting week 2's page mix on week 1's per-page rates reproduces the whole drop, so the extra traffic dilutes the blend.
- **The v3.4.1 checkout refactor (06-10) shows no clear effect, but I can't rule out a small one.** The old pages converted 3.09% before 06-10 and 3.17% from 06-10 to 06-12. The 95% interval on that difference is −0.98 to +0.81 percentage points, so a drop under about 0.8 points can't be excluded.
- **The session log has a gap on 06-13 and 06-14.** Sessions fall from about 760 a day to about 585, with mobile dropping from 440 to 242. Orders for those days are 23 and 17, but only 17 and 11 sessions reached checkout, which can't happen if the sessions were all recorded. That also explains why week-2 orders (137) exceed checkout-reached sessions (125). There is no independent session counter, so I can't confirm the gap against anything.
- **The desktop dip is most likely the new page, not a separate problem.** Desktop fell from 3.36% to 2.22%, and 364 of the new page's sessions were on desktop. I didn't test this separately.

**Limitations**
- Orders carry no session, page or device field, so I used checkout-reached rates by page and can't attribute orders to pages.
- I can't tell whether the new page's visitors are simply a different, lower-intent audience or whether the page itself converts poorly. Pausing the page, or sending a random share of traffic to it, would separate the two.
